scope: Static review of frozen MotionFeatures.inl and MotionGuardTests.cpp, native ABI/lifecycle validation, complete function evidence and source fingerprints. No product edits, build, game execution, UI actions or IDB writes by reviewer.
verdict: No remaining significant defect identified in the frozen reviewed scope. Concrete ownership, transition and callback concurrency findings are resolved. Runtime integration remains unverified by this review.
confirmedContract: Speed is float Actor+680 (embedded controller Actor+344, member+336). Native motion advancement uses delta*speed; ordinary motion changes retain this actor field.
Enable and explicit rate change write once; Tick observes ownership and validity rather than continuously forcing the speed. Supported desired range is policy 0.1..3, not an engine safety proof.

Lease binds the current living Sora actor, status/backlink, controller owner, form, scene/room, heap, both schedulers, model, model resource and resource vtable. Normal motion changes on the same model can retain the lease.

Native VM writer 0x14042FCE0 synchronously consumes an 8-byte operand array through RCX, double-decodes operand0 to Actor, and copies the float at args+8 into Actor+680. Bank1/index107 is the 16-byte table entry at RVA0x755A20.
Callback slot changes use exact native-to-own and own-to-native CAS. Original callback is immutable, bridge is pinned, and already-dispatched callbacks forward exactly once after removal.

A private exclusive SRW lock serializes callback observation plus Original with Start, rate-update and Stop field mutations. The wrapper marks ownership before native write even for the same float or expired host, and finally releases the lock when exceptions propagate.

Restore requires a freshly resolved current/listed Actor in a stable scene, matching identities, fresh table/owned slot, no observed script ownership and exact last-written bits. Lost actor/form/scene or callback/bank ownership abandons restoration.
Model or motion-resource invalidity can compare-restore only on the same valid current actor because speed belongs to Actor. Restore does not follow an old retained actor pointer.
Readouts use validated current Motion/resource data without invoking pose/evaluation mutators. No seek, arbitrary motion-ID write or zero-speed freeze was introduced.

resolvedFindings.problem: Restore originally lacked full ScenePhase checks and could run while transition globals still referred to the old scene.
resolvedFindings.resolution: CurrentOwner now requires stable ScenePhase; unready/reset contexts do not restore.

resolvedFindings.problem: Clearing observedActor before restore could hide a concurrent same-float script write and overwrite native ownership.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Observation plus native Original and all trainer field mutations share one SRW lock; observation is cleared after the restore decision.

resolvedFindings.problem: Callback/bank loss could still restore through direct Reset or HostExpired paths before MotionTick.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Stop checks TableReady and OwnSlot under the lock on every restoration path. Direct Reset and expiry cases have dedicated tests.

resolvedFindings.problem: Pre-lock host/table validation could become stale while Start or rate update waited for a callback.
resolvedFindings.resolution: Start and rate update revalidate host, table, owned slot and relevant actor/value state inside the mutation lock.

resolvedFindings.problem: Model resource pointer equality alone did not notice a changed resource vtable.
resolvedFindings.resolution: The resource vtable is included in lease identity and covered by a synthetic ownership test.

reviewedTests: Prototype and RAW readouts, normal motion changes, explicit enable/update/disable, repeat-enable baseline preservation and field pause.
Same-value and different-value script writes; unrelated actor writer; same-value writer before direct reset or host expiry.
Concurrent writer-versus-reset ordering using thread events; exactly one native call; exception propagation and lock release.
Slot/bank/code/metadata changes, foreign hook preservation, failed protection/pinning/CAS paths, resident forwarder after removal and retry.
Direct Reset and HostExpired after lost bank/slot with no restoration, including paths before normal Tick.
Wrong thread, stale/unready scene, room/heap/scheduler/form/actor/status/owner changes, model/resource/vtable changes and resource invalidity.
Invalid ranges/nonfinite values, malformed headers or lists, unreadable/unwritable data and read-only snapshot/capability paths.
limitations: No independent build or live game test was run in this review; author-reported synthetic results are attributed explicitly.
Scoped direct-writer searches do not prove absence of computed aliases, whole-object copies, arbitrary external mod writes or future code changes.
The SRW lock serializes this wrapper and trainer mutations. It cannot serialize unknown direct writers that do not use the wrapper.
Identical raw writes outside the observed VM callback and identity ABA changes between observations may be undetectable.
The exact native callback body has no observed recursive callback path. Reentrancy introduced by unrelated runtime code changes is outside the validated build contract.
Animation speed also affects root motion and trigger timing, so the option changes gameplay behavior, not only visual playback.
Synthetic memory fixtures exercise the intended guards and actual Windows SRW/CAS/protection operations but do not establish all live actor-lifetime assumptions.
